지금.e: Sino-Korean, literally 'just now' — today it simply means 'now'.
지금.t: Often used like an adverb with no particle: 지금 가요 'I'm going now'.

값.e: Spelled with ㅄ. 밥값 = meal cost.
값.t: Pronounced [갑]; before a vowel the ㅅ returns as ㅆ: 값이 [갑씨], 값을 [갑쓸].

날씨.x: The weather is really nice today.
날씨.e: Built on 날 (day): the day's condition. 날씨가 좋아요 = the weather's nice.
날씨.t: Ask about weather with 날씨가 어때요? (How's the weather?)

오다.t: Rain and snow 'come' in Korean: 비가 와요 = it's raining, 눈이 와요 = it's snowing.

들어오다.m: to come in, to enter; to come home
들어오다.x: It's cold, so come inside quickly.
들어오다.e: 들다 (enter) + 오다 (come); compare 들어가다 (go in) and 나오다 (come out).

조심하다.m: to be careful, to watch out
조심하다.ex: 눈이 와서 길이 미끄러우니까 운전 조심하세요.
조심하다.x: It snowed and the roads are slippery, so drive carefully.
조심하다.e: Literally 'hold the heart': keep your mind in check.
조심하다.t: 조심히 가세요 ('Get home safely') is a common, caring way to say goodbye.

발음.ex: 한국 친구가 제 발음이 좋다고 했어요.
발음.x: My Korean friend said my pronunciation is good.

빌려주다.x: My friend lent me an umbrella.
빌려주다.e: 빌리다 'to borrow' plus 주다 'to give' — borrowing given to someone.
빌려주다.t: 빌려주다 is to lend — a very common mix-up.

문자.ex: 집에 도착하면 저에게 문자 보내 주세요.
문자.x: Please send me a text when you get home.
문자.e: Literally 'written characters'; short for 문자 메시지 'text message'.
문자.t: Pronounced [문짜]; the usual verb is 문자를 보내다 'send a text'.

프로그램.ex: 제가 제일 좋아하는 프로그램은 요리 프로그램이에요.
프로그램.x: My favorite program is a cooking show.
프로그램.e: From English 'program'; Korean adds vowels, so it has four syllables.
프로그램.t: Often shortened to 프로 in speech: 요리 프로, 예능 프로.

냄비.x: Put water in a big pot and bring it to a boil.

이해.ex: 설명을 들어도 이해가 잘 안 돼요.
이해.x: Even after hearing the explanation, I don't really get it.
이해.t: 이해가 안 돼요 ('I don't get it') is more natural than 이해 못 해요 in many situations.

비판하다.x: The newspaper strongly criticized the government's decision.

재난.x: When a disaster happens, you should evacuate calmly.

교류.ex: 두 나라는 문화 교류를 활발하게 하고 있어요.
교류.x: The two countries are actively engaged in cultural exchange.

시즌.m: season (of a series); season (time of year)
시즌.x: Season 2 of that drama is coming out soon.
시즌.t: Also used for times of year: 휴가 시즌 'vacation season', 시즌 한정 'seasonal limited edition'.

어휴.m: ugh, phew, sigh (frustration, tiredness or relief)
어휴.ex: 어휴, 오늘 일이 왜 이렇게 많아요?
어휴.x: Ugh, why is there so much work today?
어휴.e: Imitates a long sigh. 휴 alone is more often a sigh of relief.
어휴.t: Mostly shows frustration or exhaustion, so it can sound like complaining; be careful in front of superiors.

이기주의.ex: 지나친 이기주의는 사회 문제를 만들 수 있어요.
이기주의.x: Too much selfishness can create social problems.
이기주의.t: In everyday speech the adjective 이기적이다 'to be selfish' is much more common.

한파.x: A cold snap hit suddenly, and the water pipes froze.

외교.ex: 두 나라는 외교 관계를 다시 시작했어요.
외교.x: The two countries resumed diplomatic relations.

주민 등록.ex: 이사하면 새 주소로 주민 등록을 옮겨야 해요.
주민 등록.x: When you move, you have to transfer your resident registration to the new address.
주민 등록.e: Literally 'registering the people who live here'.
주민 등록.t: Pronounced [주민등녹] — ㄹ after the ㅇ of 등 becomes [ㄴ].

출입국.m: immigration, entry and departure (of a country)
출입국.ex: 비자 문제로 출입국 관리 사무소에 다녀왔어요.
출입국.x: I went to the immigration office about a visa problem.
출입국.e: Literally 'going out of and into the country'.

가엾다.ex: 길에서 떨고 있는 강아지가 너무 가엾었어요.
가엾다.x: The puppy shivering on the street was so pitiful.
가엾다.t: 가엽다 is also standard; it is ㅂ irregular: 가여워요, 가여운.

제때.forms: 제때(에) + verb: 제때 먹다, 제때 내다
제때.m: on time, at the right time
제때.ex: 건강을 위해 밥을 제때 먹어야 해요.
제때.x: For your health, you should eat meals at the proper times.

유일하다.ex: 그는 우리 팀에서 유일하게 중국어를 할 수 있어요.
유일하다.x: He's the only one on our team who can speak Chinese.
유일하다.t: Very often used as the adverb 유일하게 ('the only one who...') or the modifier 유일한 ('the only').

첫인상.x: That person made a really good first impression.
첫인상.e: 첫 (first) + 인상: literally 'the image first stamped' on your mind.
첫인상.t: Pronounced [처딘상]: the ㅅ of 첫 becomes a ㄷ sound before linking to 인.

빌라.ex: 저는 회사 근처 빌라에 살고 있어요.
빌라.x: I live in a low-rise apartment building near my office.
빌라.e: From English 'villa'. Konglish surprise: not a luxury house, but a small low-rise building of units.
빌라.t: A 빌라 is usually four or five floors without a large complex, cheaper than an 아파트.

조문.x: I went to the funeral hall to pay my respects.
조문.t: At a Korean funeral hall, wear dark clothes and bring condolence money in a white envelope.

오싹오싹.ex: 공포 영화를 보는데 소름이 오싹오싹 돋았어요.
오싹오싹.x: I got chills all over while watching the horror movie.
오싹오싹.e: 의태어 (manner word) for the body shrinking and shivering from cold or fear.
오싹오싹.t: Pronounced [오싸고싹]: the ㄱ batchim links to the next vowel. Single 오싹하다 is common: 오싹한 이야기 'a chilling story'.

담보.x: I borrowed money from the bank using my house as collateral.
담보.t: Common pattern: N을 담보로 (using N as collateral).

조세.ex: 조세 제도를 더 공정하게 바꿔야 한다는 의견이 많습니다.
조세.x: Many people think the tax system should be made fairer.
조세.e: Formal umbrella term for taxes, used in law and policy.
조세.t: Everyday speech uses 세금; 조세 appears in laws, policy and news, e.g. 조세 정책.

유효.ex: 이 쿠폰은 이번 달 말까지 유효합니다.
유효.x: This coupon is valid until the end of this month.
유효.t: 유효 기간 is what you see on cards and coupons: the period during which they're valid.

연재되다.m: to be serialized, to run as a series
연재되다.x: That webtoon was serialized for three years.
연재되다.e: Literally 'published in connection', one part after another.

격동기.x: He lived through the turbulent years of modern Korean history.

기재하다.m: to write down, to fill in, to record (on a form or document)
기재하다.ex: 신청서에 이름과 연락처를 정확히 기재해 주세요.
기재하다.x: Please write your name and contact information accurately on the application.
기재하다.e: Literally 'record and load onto' — putting information on a document.
기재하다.t: You'll see it on forms: 아래 사항을 기재하십시오 'fill in the following.'

심혈을 기울이다.m: to put one's heart and soul into, to pour all one's effort into
심혈을 기울이다.ex: 그는 이 작품에 3년 동안 심혈을 기울였어요.
심혈을 기울이다.x: He poured his heart and soul into this work for three years.
심혈을 기울이다.e: Literally 'tilt your heart's blood' toward something — giving it everything.

이성적.x: Even when I'm angry, I try to judge things rationally.
이성적.t: Homonym alert: 이성 can also mean 'the opposite sex', as in 이성 친구 (boyfriend or girlfriend).

야심.ex: 그는 대통령이 되겠다는 야심을 숨기지 않았어요.
야심.x: He didn't hide his ambition to become president.
야심.e: Literally 'wild heart' — ambition that can't be tamed.
야심.t: 야심 can sound scheming, but 야심 차다 / 야심작 ('ambitious work') are positive.

애써.forms: 애써 + 웃다/참다/외면하다 (forcing oneself) · 애써 만든 (made with effort)
애써.m: with great effort; forcing oneself, deliberately
애써.ex: 그녀는 슬펐지만 애써 웃으며 손을 흔들었어요.
애써.x: She was sad, but she forced a smile and waved.
애써.e: From 애쓰다 'to make an effort' — 애 'worry, effort' plus 쓰다 'to use'.
애써.t: 애써 웃다 means forcing a smile, while 애써 만든 means 'made with great effort'.

고루.x: You need to eat all the side dishes evenly to stay healthy.
고루.e: Shorter partner of 골고루 'evenly'; same meaning, slightly more written.
고루.t: Unrelated to 고루하다 'old-fashioned, narrow-minded', a Sino-Korean adjective.

노심초사.x: My mother was worried sick that her son might get hurt.
노심초사.e: Literally 'toiling the mind and scorching one's thoughts.'
노심초사.t: Often paired with -(으)ㄹ까 봐: 늦을까 봐 노심초사하다 'to fret that one might be late.'

소탐대실.m: penny-wise and pound-foolish; losing big by chasing small gains
소탐대실.ex: 싼 제품만 고르다가 돈을 더 쓰게 되면 소탐대실이에요.
소탐대실.x: If you only pick cheap products and end up spending more, that's penny-wise and pound-foolish.
소탐대실.e: Literally 'covet the small, lose the big.'

발목이 잡히다.forms: 발목이 잡혀요 · 발목이 잡혔어요 · ~에 발목이 잡히다
발목이 잡히다.m: to be held back; to be tied down by something
발목이 잡히다.ex: 부상에 발목이 잡혀서 올해 대회에 못 나갔어요.
발목이 잡히다.x: I was held back by an injury and couldn't compete this year.
발목이 잡히다.e: Literally 'to be caught by the ankle.'

이면.m: the other side, the hidden side, what lies behind
이면.ex: 화려한 성공의 이면에는 많은 노력이 있었어요.
이면.x: Behind the glamorous success there was a lot of hard work.
이면.e: Literally 'inner side' or 'back side' — what's behind the surface.
이면.t: Don't confuse with the ending -(이)면 'if'; this noun usually appears as ~의 이면에(는).

후폭풍.ex: 그 정치인의 발언은 큰 후폭풍을 불러왔어요.
후폭풍.x: That politician's remark caused a huge backlash.
후폭풍.e: Literally 'the storm after': the blast that follows an explosion.

단가.ex: 원자재 가격이 올라서 제품 단가도 올랐습니다.
단가.x: Raw material prices rose, so the unit price of the product went up too.
단가.e: Literally 'single price': the price of one unit.
단가.t: Pronounced [단까]; 단가를 낮추다 means 'to cut the unit cost'.

푸념.m: grumbling, complaining; a lament over one's lot
푸념.ex: 친구는 만날 때마다 회사 일로 푸념을 늘어놓아요.
푸념.x: Every time we meet, my friend goes on and on complaining about work.
푸념.e: Native Korean; originally the words a shaman spoke in a ritual, later 'venting one's grievances'.
푸념.t: Common collocations: 푸념을 늘어놓다 (go on grumbling) and 푸념을 듣다 (listen to someone vent).
rel: tearful appeal, pouring out one's troubles

포로.ex: 양측은 전쟁이 끝난 뒤 포로를 교환했습니다.
포로.x: Both sides exchanged prisoners after the war ended.

비탄.x: The families fell into grief at the news of the accident.
비탄.t: Typical collocation: 비탄에 빠지다 / 잠기다 — to sink into grief.

구슬프다.ex: 밤에 들리는 피리 소리가 너무 구슬퍼요.
구슬프다.x: The sound of the flute at night is so mournful.
구슬프다.e: Contains 슬프다 'sad'; used mainly for sounds like songs, cries or rain.
구슬프다.t: Typically describes sounds: 구슬픈 노래, 구슬픈 목소리, 구슬프게 울다.

쿼크.ex: 양성자는 세 개의 쿼크로 이루어져 있습니다.
쿼크.x: A proton is made up of three quarks.

알레고리.ex: 조지 오웰의 동물농장은 정치를 풍자한 알레고리예요.
알레고리.x: George Orwell's Animal Farm is an allegory satirizing politics.
알레고리.e: From English 'allegory'; the Korean literary term is 풍유 or 우의.

벼슬.ex: 그는 과거에 급제해서 높은 벼슬에 올랐어요.
벼슬.x: He passed the state exam and rose to a high government post.
벼슬.e: Native word for an official post; colloquially also a rooster's comb (닭 벼슬).
벼슬.t: The typical collocation is 벼슬에 오르다, 'to rise to an official post'.

세자.ex: 세자는 어릴 때부터 왕이 되기 위한 교육을 받았어요.
세자.x: From childhood, the crown prince was trained to become king.
세자.e: Literally 'son of the generation', the heir who continues the line.

가훈.x: Our family motto is 'Let's live honestly.'
가훈.t: Korean schoolkids are often asked to write their 가훈; it's typically framed and hung at home.

견원지간.ex: 두 사람은 견원지간이라서 만나기만 하면 싸워요.
견원지간.x: Those two fight like cats and dogs whenever they meet.
견원지간.e: Literally 'the relationship between a dog and a monkey.'
견원지간.t: English says 'cats and dogs'; Korean pairs a dog with a monkey.

다사다난.m: being eventful and full of difficulties
다사다난.x: An eventful year is drawing to a close.
다사다난.t: A year-end cliché: 다사다난했던 한 해를 보내며 'saying goodbye to an eventful year'.

정보격차.ex: 노인과 젊은 세대 사이의 정보격차가 커지고 있습니다.
정보격차.x: The information gap between seniors and young people is growing.

서늘하다.x: Now that it's fall, the wind has turned cool in the mornings and evenings.
서늘하다.e: A softer cousin of 싸늘하다 'icy cold'; compare 선선하다 'pleasantly cool'.
서늘하다.t: Figurative: 등골이 서늘하다 'a chill runs down my spine' from fear.

스산하다.m: bleak, dreary, chilly and gloomy; (mind) unsettled
스산하다.ex: 비 오는 밤이라 골목길 분위기가 스산했어요.
스산하다.x: It was a rainy night, so the alley felt bleak and eerie.

지레.ex: 해 보기도 전에 지레 포기하지 마세요.
지레.x: Don't give up before you've even tried.
지레.t: Usually negative — acting too early: 지레 겁먹다 'to get scared beforehand'.

파안대소.ex: 할머니는 어린 손자의 엉뚱한 말에 파안대소하셨어요.
파안대소.x: Grandma burst out laughing at her little grandson's silly remark.
파안대소.e: Literally 'face breaking open in a big laugh.'
